turns.t: Doctor, it's my mother's legs. They've swollen up again, and she sits in the wheelchair all day now.
Thank you, I'm glad you came together. Mrs Pillai, can you tell me about the swelling?
Both my legs are swollen, from the feet to the knees.
When did you first notice it?
I don't remember. My daughter noticed it first.
I think it was around the festival, but I can't be sure. It might have been earlier.
Is it worse at any time of day?
In the evenings. By the morning it is a bit less.
Is there pain, redness or any warmth in the legs?
No, no redness. She says it just feels heavy.
Does she have any health problems that we should know about?
She has had heart failure for years, and high blood pressure.
Is she taking her water tablet regularly?
Yes, I take the water tablet.
She does, mostly, but I only see her in the evenings. Her carer gives the morning ones, and she sometimes refuses.
And which water tablet is that, and what dose?
Furosemide, 40 milligrams, once in the morning.
Do you have any allergies to medicines, Mrs Pillai?
Penicillin. It gave me a rash once.
Thank you. I'll note that. Is she short of breath lying flat?
No, she sleeps with two pillows as she always has.
I'd like to look at her legs and listen to her chest. Could you help me lift the footrest? ~
Yes, of course.
There is pitting swelling of both lower legs up to the knees, and no redness.
Is it bad, doctor? ~
It's a fluid build-up. With her heart condition and sitting all day, that's the usual cause.
Should we change her tablets? ~
I would like to increase the furosemide to 40 milligrams twice a day, morning and early afternoon, and I'll prescribe that.
We'll make sure the carer knows. ~
Please keep her legs raised when she is resting, and encourage her to take the tablets.
I will. ~
I would also like a blood test to check her kidneys and salts, since we are changing the dose.
When should we do that? ~
Within the week. Then I'll see her again once the results are in. ~
Thank you, doctor. ~
